memory_update.text: CAMT should remain high in the underfollowed lane for HBM/advanced-packaging inspection because it has disclosed recent HBM and tier-1 OSAT AI-related orders; next layer should verify durability of orders, customer concentration, and margin impact.

FORM is a plausible HBM test chokepoint candidate through probe cards and known-good-die test; prioritize verification of HBM-specific revenue mix and whether HBM4/HBM5 creates incremental probe-card upgrade cycles.
KLIC is a narrower bonding-equipment hypothesis: strong fit to heterogeneous integration and TCB, but direct HBM process exposure needs more evidence before promotion beyond Layer 1.

Amkor, Onto Innovation, ASE, substrate suppliers, thermal-material vendors, precision chemical suppliers, and HBM producers remain important adjacent names, but were excluded due to the four-candidate cap and should be revisited in later passes.
FORM should be tracked as a direct HBM test-interface candidate; key validation is HBM-specific probe-card revenue, customer concentration, and margin contribution.
CAMT should be tracked as an advanced-packaging and HBM inspection/metrology candidate; verify revenue mix and customer concentration before promoting beyond Layer 1.
ONTO is a larger-cap but still specialized process-control candidate for HBM and advanced packaging; keep as an underfollowed-quality comparator rather than a pure small-cap discovery name.
KLIC is a lower-attention hypothesis around thermocompression bonding and AI advanced packaging; requires stronger evidence on materiality and HBM-specific demand.

For the HBM upstream-input node, the most actionable US-listed sub-layers found in this pass are probe/test, inspection/metrology, and advanced bonding equipment rather than the HBM producers themselves.

Still need a separate materials/chemicals pass for underfill, bonding films, substrates, thermal interface materials, specialty gases, and ultra-pure chemicals; US-listed pure plays may be harder to identify and may sit inside diversified suppliers.

FORM should be tracked as an HBM wafer-probe and known-good-die test candidate; direct evidence exists in company materials and filings, but revenue materiality and customer concentration need verification.
ONTO is a high-quality but less underfollowed large-cap exception for HBM4 inspection/metrology; Dragonfly G5 and 3Di order commitments make it one of the cleaner node mappings.
COHU is the most small/mid-cap underfollowed HBM inspection/test candidate in this pass; HBM revenue is still small, so survival in later layers depends on follow-on orders and materiality.

AMKR belongs in the reference lane for US-listed advanced-packaging capacity, but it is less obscure and above the preferred $10B cap range; use mainly as a context anchor unless customer/capex evidence sharpens.

For the HBM advanced-packaging inputs node, the strongest US-listed underfollowed sub-nodes found in this pass are wafer probe cards, HBM inspection/metrology, package test handlers/contactors, and OSAT advanced-packaging capacity.

Need a later pass on materials and substrates: ABF, temporary bonding/debonding, thermal interface materials, photoresists, electroplating chemistries, glass substrates, and advanced substrate suppliers may be non-US-listed or hidden inside conglomerates.

CAMT should remain in the HBM/advanced-packaging inspection watchlist because recent company evidence explicitly links Hawk system orders to AI, HBM, chiplets, hybrid bonding, and high micro-bump-count wafers.
ONTO should remain in the HBM/advanced-packaging metrology watchlist, with the key evidence gap being whether HBM4 Dragonfly G5 adoption broadens beyond one leading HBM manufacturer.

FORM should remain in the HBM/advanced-packaging test watchlist because known-good-die and micro-bump/interposer testing are structurally important as HBM stack and heterogeneous-integration complexity rises.

Potentially relevant US-listed names not included due to the four-candidate limit but worth a later pass include AMKR for outsourced advanced packaging/test capacity, MKSI for Atotech plating/advanced-packaging process technology, ENTG for specialty materials/contamination control, and KLIC for advanced bonding equipment.

For this node, the strongest underfollowed subcategories appear to be inspection/metrology, probe-card wafer test, bonding, plating/chemistry, and outsourced advanced-packaging/test capacity rather than the already-visible HBM producers.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the US-listed universe for the HBM and advanced-packaging upstream-input node using a two-lane funnel. TSM is included as the obvious reference anchor because CoWoS/3DFabric capacity is structurally tied to AI accelerator packaging and HBM integration. The discovery lane emphasizes narrower inspection, metrology, probe-card, and bonding-equipment suppliers where qualification cycles, tool-of-record status, throughput limits, and customer concentration may create chokepoints beneath the already well-known HBM producers. Expanded the US-listed universe for HBM and advanced-packaging upstream inputs with a two-lane structure. Reference context remains HBM producers, TSMC/CoWoS, and AI accelerator customers, but this pass prioritizes smaller or niche equipment/test/inspection suppliers where HBM growth creates qualification-gated demand. The strongest candidates in this pass are probe-card/test interface, inspection/metrology, and thermocompression/advanced-packaging assembly equipment vendors. No buy/sell recommendation is implied. Expanded the US-listed universe for HBM and advanced-packaging upstream inputs with one context/reference OSAT and three underfollowed equipment/test/inspection suppliers. The discovery edge is less about the already-priced HBM producers and more about qualification-gated inspection, wafer probe, package test, and advanced-packaging capacity where customer ramps can create narrow chokepoints.
